Messages.Author: James Puzzo
Messages.Body:
Tom, please clarify the following:

From the original RTR in November, I thought that it was made quite clear
that the restrictions on Non-Camarillas were the following:

They couldn't become princes.

They couldn't be named Archons or Camarilla Exemp.

They can't call the following votes: praxis seizures, justicar
retribution, command of the harpies, a vote to burn Elysium:
the Arboretum.

By definition, this would exclude Non-Camarillas from calling
Prince/Justicar/IC member only votes.

By inference, I would imagine that they also cannot call Camarilla
Exemp. as it is a Camarilla type vote (but I could be wrong).

NOWHERE in this ruling does it forbid Non-Camarillas from calling votes
which are not expressly forbidden. However, rumors have spread that you
have stated that non-camarillas CAN NOT vote.

Please explain the truth with reference to definitive rulings.

Until you do so, I would urge others to follow a guide similar to the one
below which I have constructed based on the definitions in the 11/10/95 ruling:
(I apologize for anything that I left out or placed incorrectly... feel free
to email a critique...)

some of the oldest clans -- their decision to NOT join the Camarilla when
it formed does not detract from their ability to influence their Kindred
in Non-Camarilla matters and to bring such matters to a vote)

Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
James Puzzo <jam...@gw.digibd.com> wrote:
>From the original RTR in November, I thought that it was made quite clear
>that the restrictions on Non-Camarillas were the following:
> They couldn't become princes.
> They couldn't be named Archons or Camarilla Exemp.
> They can't call the following votes: praxis seizures, justicar
> retribution, command of the harpies, a vote to burn Elysium:
> the Arboretum.
>
>By definition, this would exclude Non-Camarillas from calling
>Prince/Justicar/IC member only votes.

Right.

>By inference, I would imagine that they also cannot call Camarilla
>Exemp. as it is a Camarilla type vote (but I could be wrong).

Correct.

>NOWHERE in this ruling does it forbid Non-Camarillas from calling votes
>which are not expressly forbidden. However, rumors have spread that you
>have stated that non-camarillas CAN NOT vote.

Did I say that? Bleah! If so, then sorry; there is no general prohibition
on Non-Cam vampires taking political actions. (I must have been battling
the Baltimore netcom site for connect time when I said that.)

>Votes I'm not sure about because they may or may not be ruled to be Camarilla
>specific:

>Brujah Justicar...

There's nothing really stopping a Non-Cam vampire from lobbying for
another vampire to become Justicar, so they can call these votes.

>The vote to burn: Masquerade Enforcement

Hm. I don't remember whether we discussed that one or not. Seems simpler
to let them do it, though.
